extracted.intended_audience: Treasury witnessing officers; veterans requesting adjusted service bond payments; Indian Service officials, superintendents, regional foresters, tribal representatives, and timber purchasers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulations governing management, development, sale, and protection of timber on Indian reservations, plus Treasury rules authorizing and describing witnessing/certification procedures for assignments and adjusted service bond payments. Covers policy objectives, sale procedures, contracts, bonds, payments, permits, conservation, and reservation-specific statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officers to witness assignments (Treasury)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the Treasury Department officers authorized to witness assignments of United States registered bonds and notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named officers include: Secretary of the Treasury; Under Secretary; Assistant Secretaries; Commissioner, Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner of the Public Debt; Chief and Assistant Chief of the Division of Loans and Currency; Treasurer, Assistant Treasurer, and Executive Assistant to the Treasurer. "No other officers in the Treasury Department at Washington are authorized to witness the assignments."

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnessing officer certification requirements (Treasury)
rubrics_metrics.description: The witnessing officer must certify that the person executing the assignment appeared personally before him; was known or proved to be the payee of the particular security assigned or his duly constituted assign; and that such person executed the transfer, acknowledging it to be his free act and deed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnessing officers are held strictly accountable and expected to respond for losses from want of care. The witnessing officer must affix official signature, title, address, and the date of assignment to the assignment certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officers to witness/certify requests for adjusted service bond payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the Treasury officers authorized to witness and certify requests for payment by the Treasurer of Adjusted Service Bonds (mirrors authorized officers for registered issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the same core Treasury officers as for assignments; additionally authorizes certain agency officers to witness/certify requests made by veterans employed in specified services (e.g., Chief Clerk and Superintendent for the Department generally; Head or Acting Head, Personnel Division for Bureau of Internal Revenue; Chief Accountant and Assistant Chief Accountant for Bureau of Engraving and Printing; Administrative Assistant, Branch of Supply for Procurement Division).

rubrics_metrics.name: Witnessing/certifying officer requirements for adjusted service bonds
rubrics_metrics.description: The witnessing officer must certify that the person signing the request for payment appeared personally before him and was known or proved to be the payee of the particular bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifying officers are held to strict accountability for losses from want of care; the witnessing officer must affix official signature, title, address, and date of certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy objectives for Indian forests
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives include preservation of Indian forest lands in a perpetually productive state, development by the Indian people to promote self-sustaining Indian communities, and sale of timber in open competitive markets when annual volume exceeds practical Indian development or damage requires rapid harvesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Development aims to provide Indians stumpage and other benefits and employment. Management must balance production, protection, and community benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained yield requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In conformity with the act (36 Stat. 857, Sec. 7), no Indian timber may be developed either by Indians or by others unless it is operated on a sustained yield basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement is foundational and applies to all timber development under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development by Indians — authorization and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian logging and sawmill operations may be organized and initiated for development by the Indians to promote self-sustaining communities, subject to the consent of the Indians in general council and availability of funds (appropriations, loans, tribal funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations may be supported by general appropriations, special appropriations for sawmill development, reimbursable loan funds, or Indian tribal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber Sale Law — Secretary-prescribed regulations and proceeds use
rubrics_metrics.description: Mature living and dead and down timber on unallotted lands of any Indian reservation may be sold under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Interior; proceeds used for the benefit of the Indians of the reservation as he may direct (with statutory exceptions for some states).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section notes exceptions (States of Minnesota and Wisconsin) and references statutory authority; also addresses sale of timber on allotments held under restricted patents with Secretary's consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales from unallotted and allotted lands — consent and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales on reservations where timber volume exceeds Indian development capacity, or where stands are deteriorating, will be authorized provided consent is given by Indians in general council (or authorized representatives) for tribal lands and by allottees for allotted lands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sales with stumpage value over $100 will not be authorized until examined by a qualified forest officer and a complete report submitted to approving officer(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of sales — methods and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All sales of timber of stumpage value greater than $100 shall be made only after due advertisement and under sealed bids; manner and duration of advertisement depend on stumpage value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stumpage ≤ $1,000, advertisement may be by posters and circular letters; if > $1,000, advertisement must be in at least one local newspaper. Advertisement durations: ≤ $10,000 — not less than 15 days; > $10,000 and ≤ $100,000 — not less than 30 days; > $100,000 — not less than 60 days. Approving officer must approve advertisement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposits with bids — percentages and form
rubrics_metrics.description: A cash deposit is required with each proposal; deposit percentages vary by estimated stumpage value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit rates: < $1,000 — at least 20%; $1,000–$10,000 — at least 10%; $10,000–$100,000 — at least 5%; > $100,000 — at least 3%. Deposits > $500 must be a certified check on a solvent national bank payable to the superintendent; smaller deposits may be cash or certified check. Deposits guarantee good faith and are retained until contract completion if no bond is executed; successful bidder's deposit credited toward payment; returned to unsuccessful bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and rejection of bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily the high bid received shall be accepted, but the approving officer may reject the high bid and readvertise if the high bidder is considered unqualified; approving officer may waive minor technical defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approving officer has discretion to ensure contractual requirements can be met and to maintain sale integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales to Indians without advertisement (small sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-market sales to Indians without advertising may be made for stumpage not exceeding $5,000 in value, with requisite tribal/allottee consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stumpage prices for such sales are established by the approving officer after appraisal; contract forms and bond requirements per Section 14 and 16 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts — required forms and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: For sales > $100 stumpage value, regular contract forms must be used unless a special form is approved by Commissioner of Indian Affairs or Secretary of the Interior; specific form numbers are prescribed for different sale types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form guidance: form 5-487 for unallotted lands sold to Indians/others; form 5-489 for allotted lands; form 5-481 for logging operations conducted by an Indian. Contracts must be executed in sextuplet by authorized tribal representatives/allottees and purchaser. If approved by superintendent (or superintendent + regional forester) originals are forwarded to General Accounting Office and copies to Indian Office and regional forester; if higher approval required, all copies forwarded promptly to Indian Office. Copies returned for agency, regional, purchaser, and allottee files upon approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of contracts — approval authorities by value
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval authority depends on stumpage value of the sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts ≤ $500 may be approved by the superintendent. Contracts > $500 and ≤ $10,000 should be approved by the superintendent and concurred in by the regional forester (nonconcurrence appealed to Commissioner of Indian Affairs). Contracts > $10,000 and ≤ $100,000 should be approved by the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Contracts > $100,000 require express approval of the Secretary of the Interior. Individual allotment contracts under a general contract approved by higher authority may be approved by superintendent on form 5-489 with stipulated provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds — bond requirements by stumpage value
rubrics_metrics.description: Bond requirements for sales vary by stumpage value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally: stumpage ≤ $5,000 — ordinarily no bond required (initial deposit held until contract completion); > $5,000 and ≤ $10,000 — bond approximately 20% of timber value; > $10,000 and ≤ $100,000 — bond approximately 10% of estimated timber value; > $100,000 — bond amount fixed by Secretary of the Interior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments for timber — advance payments and installment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments required in advance of cutting, as single payment or installments; number of installments limited by stumpage value and specific rules for allotment sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installment limits: ≤ $1,000 — max 5 installments; > $1,000 and ≤ $10,000 — max 10 installments; > $10,000 and ≤ $100,000 — max 20 installments; > $100,000 — number determined at time of sale but installments not less than $5,000 each. For allotment contracts of ≤ 3 years, an advance payment of 10% of estimated value is stipulated; for sales >3 years further advances required. Absent special instructions, allotment contracts should provide: 10% within 30 days of approval, an additional 15% within 3 years, and a further 25% within 6 years; advances credited against timber as cut and scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for cutting and removal of timber — maximum periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum allowed periods after contract date for cutting/removal depend on sale value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum periods: stumpage ≤ $1,000 — 1 year; > $1,000 and ≤ $10,000 — 3 years; > $10,000 and ≤ $100,000 — 8 years; > $100,000 — number of years fixed in advertisement. Distribution of cutting over allowed period must not make supervision unreasonably costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction for administrative purposes and accounting for proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: A deduction will be made from gross proceeds to cover costs of examination, supervision, advertising, collecting, disbursing, accounting, marking, scaling, slash care, and fire protection; accounting for proceeds must show tribal, individual, and deductions separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless special instructions given, 8% of gross amount from sales under regular supervision will be deducted to cover administrative expenses (act of Feb. 14, 1920). If timber sold for lump sum and no subsequent administration required, 3% deduction is made. Procedures specified for receipts: when ownership known, receipts must separately show tribal fund credit, individual Indian credit, and administrative deduction; when ownership not known funds placed in special deposits until scale reports determine distribution. Proceeds from unallotted timber deposited as "sundry receipts" in Treasury; deductions credited to United States as "miscellaneous receipts"; net proceeds titled as "Indian moneys, proceeds of labor" or other applicable title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permits for limited cutting — form and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All timber cutting not under formal contract (except allotted timber cut for allottee's personal use) must be done under permit form 5-924; permits intended for limited domestic, agricultural, or grazing needs and not as substitute for contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum stumpage value permitted under permit per individual in one year is $100. Permits for unallotted timber to Indian operators for personal use may be without stumpage charge but must be under permit and trees designated by a forest officer. All permits for unallotted timber must be approved by duly authorized tribal representatives; permits for allotted timber must be approved by the allottee or their legal representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil conservation and erosion prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Soil erosion prevention should receive primary consideration in Indian forest management; heavy cuttings generally not permitted in erosion-prone areas and cuttings must protect forest and ground cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include plugging gullies with brush, scattering brush to form protective cover rather than piling/burning, locating roads/trails to minimize runoff, avoiding steep grades and unnecessary side-hill cuts, and avoiding long tangents requiring much cut/fill. Local officials should obtain expert advice where erosion problems vary widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreation and scenic preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider reserving specific areas from logging for recreational and scenic purposes; cutting along stocked streams should be conservative to protect fish habitat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve strip widths: at least 250 feet on side of all highways in ponderosa pine type and Lake States forests; in large West Coast timber reserve at least a quarter of a mile on either side of the road. In reserved strips, no trees other than dead or dying should be cut. Timber operations must not interfere with Indian ceremonial sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with special acts and reservation-specific statutes/decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The general act (June 25, 1910) does not repeal provisions of special acts applicable to particular reservations; all requirements of special acts in conflict with the general law must be complied with. Some reservations have specific statutory provisions limiting or permitting sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations under the general act will be applied where not in conflict with special acts. Examples and citations given for many reservations and special acts (e.g., Minnesota and Wisconsin exceptions; Menominee, Red Lake, Bad River, Five Civilized Tribes, etc.). Attention directed to various acts and Comptroller General decisions (e.g., Dec. 17, 1931 decision that contracts may not be legally modified to reduce payments absent express statutory authority).
